questionText: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct about the B+ tree data structure used for creating an index of a relational database table?
options: B+ Tree is a height-balanced tree
Non-leaf nodes have pointers to data records
Key values in each node are kept in sorted order
Each leaf node has a pointer to the next leaf node
explanation:
Option A: A B+ tree is always height-balanced, meaning all leaf nodes are located at the exact same level. Hence, statement (A) is correct.

Option B: In a B+ tree, data record pointers are stored exclusively at the leaf nodes. Non-leaf (internal) nodes store only search keys and node pointers to direct tree traversal. Therefore, non-leaf nodes do not contain pointers to data records. Hence, statement (B) is NOT correct.

Option C: Keys within each node are always maintained in sorted order to allow binary search during lookups. Hence, statement (C) is correct.

Option D: Leaf nodes are linked sequentially using pointers to enable efficient range queries and sequential access. Hence, statement (D) is correct.
